plotSections.title: The Eldarin Tree and the Mother's Prayer
bullets: Plymouth Gawater explains that Gerk is a 'son of a great tree' connected to the Eldarin Tree, an ancient and sacred tree of the Navi and one of Atlas's greatest magical places.
The Navi created the keystones by studying and distilling the rings of the Eldarin Tree into magical items, drawing knowledge from the tree.

The creation of the keystones unintentionally set the Mother's Prayer into motion. The resulting prophecy periodically brings forth individuals when Atlas needs them to protect the health and prosperity of the world.
Gerk's acceptance of this role is described as being 'plucked' or taken as ripe fruit from the Eldarin Tree, with his companions joining him in the resulting responsibility.

plotSections.title: Gerk Becomes the Doorman of Midgard
bullets: Gerk is offered the title of Doorman, a role not granted to anyone in many years.
The Doorman has the ability to open and close the Arch associated with their realm, reach out and connect with it, and protect it.
Gerk chooses the Keystone of Midgard/Midgar after discussing the available realms with the party.
Unlike previous keepers, who were tasked primarily with hiding and preserving their keystones, Gerk is expected to protect, actively use, and help make Midgard greater through the keystone.
Gerk formally accepts the Keystone of Midgard. A breeze passes through the cavern and white flower petals appear around him.

plotSections.title: The White-Flower Girl
bullets: The mysterious small girl the party has encountered before appears in the distant corridor after Gerk receives the Midgard keystone.
She floats above the central empty bay rather than walking along either side and leaves a trail of white flowers behind her.
Gerk, Sylan, Walker, and Plymouth can all see her, confirming that Gerk is not imagining her presence.
Gerk rolls a natural 20 on Perception and recognizes from Plymouth's demeanor that Plymouth is genuinely acknowledging the girl's presence.
Gerk wants to follow the trail of flowers immediately, but Sylan convinces him to finish the current undertaking first and promises that they will look for her afterward.
Plymouth tells Gerk that following the girl is part of Gerk's own journey rather than something Plymouth can resolve for him.

plotSections.title: The Other Keystone Keepers
bullets: Plymouth begins assigning the remaining party members their own keystones and responsibilities.
Sylan accepts the Keystone of Gilbrick, with Plymouth noting that Sylan is a child of the lord of that realm and therefore receives the first choice.
Walker is offered the Keystone of La-rel, with Plymouth explaining that Walker is the only member of the group who is not actually from Midgard.
The transcript ends immediately after Plymouth offers Walker the Keystone of La-rel, so Walker's final decision is not established in this chunk.

chronologicalEvents: The party steps forward while Gerk kneels beside Plymouth Gawater; Kit Anger and Juten Prime step back and allow events to unfold.
Plymouth explains the Eldarin Tree, its sacred importance to the Navi, and its connection to the creation of the keystones.
Plymouth reveals that creating the keystones unintentionally initiated the Mother's Prayer and its recurring prophecy.
Gerk is offered the long-unused title of Doorman, granting him responsibility for opening, closing, connecting with, and protecting an Arch.
Plymouth presents Gerk with the Keystone of Pitel, but Gerk asks about the other available realms before choosing.
The party discusses the realms, including Feldspar, Gilbrick, Lith, Turof, La-rel, the Reach, and Midgard.
Gerk chooses Midgard/Midgar and receives its keystone.
White flower petals appear as Gerk takes the Midgard keystone, and the mysterious white-flower girl appears in the distant corridor.
Gerk confirms through a natural 20 Perception check that Plymouth is genuinely acknowledging the girl's presence.
Gerk wants to follow the girl's trail of white flowers, but Sylan persuades him to wait until the current proceedings are complete.
Sylan accepts the Keystone of Gilbrick.
Plymouth offers Walker the Keystone of La-rel, noting that Walker is the only party member not actually from Midgard; the transcript ends before Walker responds.

Unlike previous keepers, Gerk is expected not only to preserve the keystone but to use it and help make Midgard greater.

newTerms.name: Eldarin Tree
notes: A great and sacred tree of the Navi and one of Atlas's greatest magical places.
The Navi used knowledge and rings from the tree in the creation of the keystones.

newTerms.name: Mother's Prayer
notes: A prophecy or self-propagating process unintentionally initiated through the creation of the keystones.
Periodically brings forth individuals needed to protect the health and prosperity of Atlas.

newTerms.name: Doorman
notes: A rare title granted to an individual responsible for opening and closing an Arch, connecting with it, and protecting it.
Gerk is granted the title and becomes the Doorman associated with Midgard.

newTerms.name: Keystone Keeper
notes: A role previously focused on hiding and preserving a keystone.
The current generation of keepers is expected to actively use and protect their keystones and improve their respective realms.

newTerms.name: Son of the Great Tree
notes: A description applied to Gerk by Plymouth, apparently referring to Gerk's connection to the Eldarin Tree.
